meta.reason_notes: key_context[key].reason says what to do with each key. missing: the key is not in your file; append it as a new line. blank, equal_to_english, english_changed: the key IS already in your file, holding key_context[key].current_value; REPLACE that value in place and never append a second line for the same key. english_changed means the English was reworded after your file's translation was written: translate the new English, and keep words from the old translation only where they still say what the new English says.
meta.placeholder_notes: A word in curly braces ({n}, {ids}, {flow}, {iterations}, {name}) is a PLACEHOLDER the page replaces at runtime. Keep every one of them, spelled exactly as in English, braces included. Never translate the word inside the braces. You MAY move a placeholder to wherever your language needs it in the sentence.
meta.control_name_notes: Where an English string names a control, it names it in one of two shapes. A single control is written as its label followed by the widget word: "press the Calculate button", "the Recalculate automatically setting", "the Required fire flow box". A menu path is written as comma-separated labels: "File, Save as"; "Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics". In BOTH shapes the label is another key's value. Translate it with exactly the words you used for that key, so the sentence still names what is on the screen; translate the widget word and the surrounding prose normally.
meta.glossary_notes: glossary lists the technical terms that the strings in this batch use, each named in plain words, with your language's preferred translation where one exists. Use the preferred translation wherever the term appears, unless your language's genuine standard term is better; then use that and say so in your report.
meta.context_notes: Use key_context[key].neighbors to keep register consistent with nearby translated strings. key_context[key].tip is the help text shown for that label, and key_context[key].label is the label a tip explains: read the pair together, and give the same thing the same word in both. Where the partner already has a translation in your file, its value is shown.
meta.plain_notes: key_plain[key] says in plain words what that one string means, other wordings joined by "or". Use whichever your language expresses most naturally and compactly; you are not bound to the literal English wording.
meta.key_notes_notes: key_notes[key] are notes about that one string: how much room it has, symbols to keep exactly, what it refers to. Follow them. They are instructions to you, never text to put in your file.
meta.suggestion_box_notes: Read suggestion_box and follow it. It is part of your instructions, not a footnote: a sprint does not close while a translator complaint is unanswered.
translator_notes: Tree, parent, child and inherit are the words of a family tree. Use the everyday family words of your language.
meta.translator_notes_notes: Read translator_notes and follow them. Each is true of every string you translate.
meta.concept_notes: Read concept_source and follow it. key_concepts lists, for a key that names a concept, its plain-words name, which is what you translate from; English is one rendering of it.
meta.uniqueness_notes: uniqueness_attention lists the few groups of concepts that sit side by side on one screen. Find unique names for each, and use each name the same way everywhere.

suggestion_box:
## Suggestion box — file a grievance about the English

If any English string made you guess, file it. You are the only person who will ever
notice, and a string that made you guess will make the next 25 translators guess too.

File an entry when: the English has more than one plausible reading; a verb or adjective
has no stated object; a word's intended sense is not its most common sense; a term maps
onto a dangerous second sense in your language; a claim in the text looks false or stale;
or the tooling handed you a preferred_translation that is wrong for the context.

Report them in your final message as a JSON array, separate from your prose:

FRICTION: [
  {"key": "<lang key>", "complaint": "<what made you guess, in one sentence>",
   "readings": ["<reading you chose>", "<reading you rejected>"]}
]

An empty array is a fine and useful answer. Do NOT invent entries -- a false one costs a
human's attention. But do not stay quiet to be agreeable either: this channel exists
because real complaints were previously buried in prose and never acted on.

Where it goes and what happens next: the orchestrator copies each entry into
dev/english-friction/<sprint>.json, adds "source": "translator" and "lang": "<your
language code>", and answers it with a "disposition" plus a written "resolution" --
english (the English was rewritten), intent, glossary, dismissed (with the reason), or
refer-to-human. refer-to-human is a real answer and does NOT close the entry: escalating
is not resolving, and it stays visible until Tom rules on it. friction_check.php blocks
the sprint from CLOSING while any entry of yours is unanswered, so filing one is expected
work that the sprint waits on -- not a complaint about the sprint.
concept_source:
## Concepts are the source

Each concept is named in plain words, with its synonyms joined by "or". That plain name
is the authoritative source; the English term is one rendering of it, as yours will be.
Where key_concepts lists a concept for a key, translate the thing the plain name
describes, and give that concept the same word in every key that cites it. Where a
concept also has a definition, it is the author's own and outranks everything else.
Where a key has no key_concepts entry, the English is the source, as before.

uniqueness_attention lists the few groups of concepts that sit side by side on one
screen. Find unique names for each.

keys_to_translate.lpn_field_tank_minvol_tip: The volume of water in the tank at its minimum depth, in the length unit cubed, for a tank with a sloped or curved bottom; 0 uses the tank diameter, and a volume curve overrides it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_tank_overflow_tip: Yes lets a full tank spill what it cannot hold, so the pipe into it stays open; No closes the pipe into a full tank. Only an extended period simulation uses it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_text_contour_box: Controls the contour plot drawn on the map from the node property chosen in Color nodes by, in the color scheme chosen in Settings, Symbology, Node colors: the fill and its opacity, how far the color reaches from each pipe, and the contour line interval and labels. With No color chosen there is no property to plot and nothing is drawn. Show plot draws or hides the plot and changes no other setting; it leaves the node colors. It changes only the display, not the network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_text_rptbox: Shows the EPANET text report of the last run, including its warnings and the network summary. Either solver writes it, for a single instant or for an extended period simulation. Each run replaces it, and an edit that does not run leaves the previous report in place.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_scn_marks_def:
On the map, an asset that has an override in the open scenario is ringed in amber, and an asset that inherits an override from a parent scenario or alternative is ringed with a dashed gray line. For demand, diameter, roughness, minor (local) loss coefficient, and length, a ring appears only while Settings, Symbology, Node labels or Link labels shows that value on the map; an override of any other property always has its ring. In Tables, a cell that holds a value set by the open scenario has the solid dot and the arrow described below at its left, and they work as they do in Properties. Its tip names the alternative that holds it, as in Physical alt.: Larger main. Show scenarios, in the cell menu of a table, lists every asset once for each scenario.

Each row of Properties that a scenario can override has a mark at its left. A solid dot means the open scenario overrides the value; click it to clear the override. An arrow over the solid dot pushes the override upward: click it, and after a confirmation that names where the value goes, it is cleared here and entered in the parent scenario. A hollow dot means the value is inherited; click it to make the value shown an override. A triangle means scenarios below this one override the value; click it to clear their overrides, after a confirmation. Beneath an overridden row is what Clear restores, as in Clear restores 18 in, the value in Base. The Settings box has the solid dot and the triangle only, because typing a value there is what makes an override.

To hide the rings, clear Show override markers on the map in Settings, Page, or choose Map, Clean map. Both are kept in this browser, not in the project. Tables marks overrides either way.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_set_where_def:
The list at the left of the box jumps to a section or a sub-heading. The sections are Symbology (Node labels, Node colors, Link labels, Link colors, Customer, and All), Map, Page, Assets (ID prefixes, Values, and Custom properties), Calculation (Solver, Units, Time, Hydraulics, Energy, and Quality), and Credits. Each sub-heading states whether its settings are Saved with the project or Saved in this browser. Everything is saved with the project except the settings under Page and one row in Solver, Show the run progress box, which states Saved in this browser itself.

The Settings tab in Tables lists the same settings as rows, with their Category and Value, so a setting can also be found and audited there.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ct_what_def: Choose Water, Graphs, Contour. The row checks Show plot in the open scenario and opens the box; the plot is drawn with the Fill and the contour lines as the box has them set, which for a new project is a smooth fill with labeled lines. The plot spreads the node colors along the pipes and up to a set multiple of the median pipe length beside them, fading out over the outer part. Its property is the one chosen in Color nodes by, in Settings, Symbology, Node colors; with No color there is nothing to plot, and the box says so. It does not color across pumps, valves, or closed links. The line under the color key states how many nodes and pipes the plot uses, the reach beside the pipes, and the interval of the lines. With too few nodes, it says so.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ct_box_def: The first line of the box states Follows project "Node colors" settings, and Node colors is a link that opens Settings at Symbology, Node colors. The plot spreads the node property chosen in Color nodes by, in the Color scheme, both there; the box has no property or scheme of its own, and a change in Settings shows in the plot at once. With No color chosen, a second line says there is nothing to plot, nothing is drawn, and the plot returns when a property is chosen again. Show plot draws or hides the plot and changes nothing else: when it is cleared, the Fill, Show contour lines, Labels, and the other settings keep their values and have no effect, and when it is checked they act as set; the node colors stay either way. The box holds the Fill (None, Smooth, or Bands, which paints each class in one solid color), the Fill opacity, the Buffer (× median pipe length), and Show contour lines, with its Interval and Labels. In a project placed on the Earth, the box can also take the ground between nodes from Mapbox DEM, after the visitor agrees to send the tile numbers of the network's area. These settings are saved with the project and can be overridden by a scenario. The plot changes only the display, not the network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_ct_example_def: Open the Net1 example, choose Settings, Symbology, Node colors, and under Color nodes by choose Pressure. Then choose Water, Graphs, Contour. The contour plot shows pressure, and the line under the color key states 9 nodes, 11 pipes, a reach of 2.5 times the median pipe length beside them, and lines every 5 psi. The pump, Link 9, is not one of the 11 pipes. The nodes keep their colors after Show plot is cleared, and the Fill and the contour lines keep their settings for when it is checked again.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_rr_what_def: Choose Water, Reports, Solver (run). The Solver (run) report is the printed report of a run in the layout and wording of the EPANET report. The row is grey until the network has been run. Either solver writes it, for a single instant or for an extended period simulation, and its header states the solver used. It starts with that header and the name of the network, then counts the junctions, reservoirs, tanks, pipes, pumps, and valves, then states the analysis options, and then lists the hydraulic status of the run with its warnings. The Copy button copies the text.
keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_rr_example_def: Open the Net1 example, which has been calculated already, and choose Water, Reports, Solver (run). The summary counts 9 junctions, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 12 pipes, 1 pump, and 0 valves. The headloss formula is Hazen-Williams, the hydraulic timestep is 1.00 hrs, and the total duration is 24.00 hrs.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ex_elm_street_desc: Background image, not georeferenced. 17 junctions, 1 reservoir, and 1 pump. A commercial site solved for fire flow on top of maximum day demand, at one moment in time, drawn over a site plan. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

keys_to_translate.lpn_file_import_msx_tip: Attach an EPANET-MSX file (.msx) to this project, or show the one already attached. It is kept with the project, written back unchanged, and run in an extended period simulation by the solver selected in Settings.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_msx_tip: The value of this EPANET-MSX species, computed by the selected solver, in the units the EPANET-MSX file declares. For a link it is the average along the link.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_headloss: This file names a head loss formula EPANET does not accept, so the pipe roughness numbers were kept as written and read as Hazen-Williams.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_report: This file contains EPANET report-format settings. The Solver (run) report is available under Reports, Solver (run), but it uses the standard EPANET format rather than the format these settings specify. The lines are kept and are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_quality_options: This file states EPANET water quality options: the Quality option, which names the kind of water quality analysis, and two settings that go with a chemical, Diffusivity and Quality tolerance. All three are kept and used. Water age, source trace, and a chemical are each computed here, and the two chemical settings are used when a chemical is run. All of them are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inpalt_lead: This file changes values in the categories below. Choose the alternative that receives the values of each.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inpalt_base_note: Every scenario inherits the Base alternative, so choosing it changes them all.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: By default the network is solved by the EPANET solver. When a total run time is set, each reporting time step is calculated in sequence: tanks fill and drain, demands follow their patterns, and the toolbar plays back the run. With Use the built-in solver selected, the network, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, is solved by the built-in solver instead. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_engine_unavailable: Could not download the EPANET solver, so the built-in solver runs this network. After one connection to the internet, the EPANET solver is stored on this device.
keys_to_translate.lpn_engine_unavailable_why: The EPANET solver could not be downloaded, so the built-in solver runs this network. {reason}
keys_to_translate.lpn_engine_needed_failed: The EPANET solver has not yet been loaded and cannot be loaded now, so the built-in solver runs this network. EPANET will be loaded when you are connected to the internet.
keys_to_translate.lpn_engine_needed_failed_why: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver runs this network. {reason}
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_viscosity_tip: EPANET reads a value above 0.001 as a ratio to the viscosity of water at 20 degrees Celsius, and a value of 0.001 or less as the kinematic viscosity itself, in ft²/s for US flow units and m²/s for SI flow units. It only changes the answer under the Darcy-Weisbach method.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_engine_native_tip: Select this to use the built-in solver. Otherwise, the EPANET solver from the US EPA is used. The built-in solver runs every network the page builds, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, and the status bar states which solver was used. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it. The first time the EPANET solver is used, about 650 KB is downloaded and then kept on this device.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_stopped: The EPANET run stopped at {time}, so it has no results. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_stopped_kept: The EPANET run stopped at {time}. Results run to {solved}, the last period it solved, and none are shown after it. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_fell_back: The numbers on screen came from the built-in solver instead. They show the network at {time} only, with every tank at its initial level.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_color_node_field_tip: Colors the nodes by this property. The contour plot follows it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_color_ramp_node_tip: Colors the nodes, the contour plot and its key.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_epanet_fallback: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver ran this network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_epanet_fallback_why: The built-in solver ran this network, because the EPANET solver could not be used. {reason}
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_report_tip: The text report of the last run: the network counts, the analysis options, whether it converged, the status of each step, and any warnings. Its header states the solver used, and both solvers use the layout and wording of the EPANET report.
keys_to_translate.lpn_quality_diffusivity_tip: EPANET reads a value above 0.0001 as a ratio to the diffusivity of chlorine in water, and a value of 0.0001 or less as the diffusivity itself, in ft²/s for US flow units and m²/s for SI flow units. Blank uses the EPANET default of 1.0.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_export_flat_label_semicolon: Texts ({n}) here contain a semicolon, and EPANET cuts a Text at its first semicolon. Each is written whole in the file, and EPANET will read only the part before the semicolon.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_demand_model_tip: Choose how junctions receive flow. Demand driven (DDA) delivers every demand in full, whatever the pressure. Pressure driven (PDA) delivers less than the demand where the pressure is below the required pressure.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_rules_refused: EPANET does not accept these rules, because a clause is not valid for the element it names or states a value that cannot be read. Correct or delete them:

keys.lpn_guide_scn_marks_def:
On the map, an asset that has an override in the open scenario is ringed in amber, and an asset that inherits an override from a parent scenario or alternative is ringed with a dashed gray line. For demand, diameter, roughness, minor (local) loss coefficient, and length, a ring appears only while Settings, Symbology, Node labels or Link labels shows that value on the map; an override of any other property always has its ring. In Tables, a cell that holds a value set by the open scenario has the solid dot and the arrow described below at its left, and they work as they do in Properties. Its tip names the alternative that holds it, as in Physical alt.: Larger main. Show scenarios, in the cell menu of a table, lists every asset once for each scenario.

Each row of Properties that a scenario can override has a mark at its left. A solid dot means the open scenario overrides the value; click it to clear the override. An arrow over the solid dot pushes the override upward: click it, and after a confirmation that names where the value goes, it is cleared here and entered in the parent scenario. A hollow dot means the value is inherited; click it to make the value shown an override. A triangle means scenarios below this one override the value; click it to clear their overrides, after a confirmation. Beneath an overridden row is what Clear restores, as in Clear restores 18 in, the value in Base. The Settings box has the solid dot and the triangle only, because typing a value there is what makes an override.

To hide the rings, clear Show override markers on the map in Settings, Page, or choose Map, Clean map. Both are kept in this browser, not in the project. Tables marks overrides either way.
keys.lpn_guide_set_where_def:
The list at the left of the box jumps to a section or a sub-heading. The sections are Symbology (Node labels, Node colors, Link labels, Link colors, Customer, and All), Map, Page, Assets (ID prefixes, Values, and Custom properties), Calculation (Solver, Units, Time, Hydraulics, Energy, and Quality), and Credits. Each sub-heading states whether its settings are Saved with the project or Saved in this browser. Everything is saved with the project except the settings under Page and one row in Solver, Show the run progress box, which states Saved in this browser itself.

The Settings tab in Tables lists the same settings as rows, with their Category and Value, so a setting can also be found and audited there.
keys.lpn_guide_ct_what_def: Choose Water, Graphs, Contour. The row checks Show plot in the open scenario and opens the box; the plot is drawn with the Fill and the contour lines as the box has them set, which for a new project is a smooth fill with labeled lines. The plot spreads the node colors along the pipes and up to a set multiple of the median pipe length beside them, fading out over the outer part. Its property is the one chosen in Color nodes by, in Settings, Symbology, Node colors; with No color there is nothing to plot, and the box says so. It does not color across pumps, valves, or closed links. The line under the color key states how many nodes and pipes the plot uses, the reach beside the pipes, and the interval of the lines. With too few nodes, it says so.
keys.lpn_guide_ct_box_def: The first line of the box states Follows project "Node colors" settings, and Node colors is a link that opens Settings at Symbology, Node colors. The plot spreads the node property chosen in Color nodes by, in the Color scheme, both there; the box has no property or scheme of its own, and a change in Settings shows in the plot at once. With No color chosen, a second line says there is nothing to plot, nothing is drawn, and the plot returns when a property is chosen again. Show plot draws or hides the plot and changes nothing else: when it is cleared, the Fill, Show contour lines, Labels, and the other settings keep their values and have no effect, and when it is checked they act as set; the node colors stay either way. The box holds the Fill (None, Smooth, or Bands, which paints each class in one solid color), the Fill opacity, the Buffer (× median pipe length), and Show contour lines, with its Interval and Labels. In a project placed on the Earth, the box can also take the ground between nodes from Mapbox DEM, after the visitor agrees to send the tile numbers of the network's area. These settings are saved with the project and can be overridden by a scenario. The plot changes only the display, not the network.
keys.lpn_guide_ct_example_def: Open the Net1 example, choose Settings, Symbology, Node colors, and under Color nodes by choose Pressure. Then choose Water, Graphs, Contour. The contour plot shows pressure, and the line under the color key states 9 nodes, 11 pipes, a reach of 2.5 times the median pipe length beside them, and lines every 5 psi. The pump, Link 9, is not one of the 11 pipes. The nodes keep their colors after Show plot is cleared, and the Fill and the contour lines keep their settings for when it is checked again.
keys.lpn_guide_rr_what_def: Choose Water, Reports, Solver (run). The Solver (run) report is the printed report of a run in the layout and wording of the EPANET report. The row is grey until the network has been run. Either solver writes it, for a single instant or for an extended period simulation, and its header states the solver used. It starts with that header and the name of the network, then counts the junctions, reservoirs, tanks, pipes, pumps, and valves, then states the analysis options, and then lists the hydraulic status of the run with its warnings. The Copy button copies the text.
keys.lpn_guide_rr_example_def: Open the Net1 example, which has been calculated already, and choose Water, Reports, Solver (run). The summary counts 9 junctions, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 12 pipes, 1 pump, and 0 valves. The headloss formula is Hazen-Williams, the hydraulic timestep is 1.00 hrs, and the total duration is 24.00 hrs.

lpn_time_run_report: Layout (box title): The title of a box that can be docked and set to auto-hide. Tucked away, the box shows only the start of its title, on a narrow tab at the map's edge turned on its side, cut off after about 12 to 25 characters. Put the word that names the box's subject first, so each tab can be told from its neighbors; a title form with a colon is fine (Pump energy report, in Spanish: Bombas: informe de energía). Where the natural phrase already starts with that word, keep it. The same text may also be a menu row.
